#### Direct Chemical Measurement Meets Simple Injection

Chemical injection is not a new concept.

For years, agricultural application equipment has used sophisticated direct-injection systems that meter concentrated products into a spray stream. Many of these systems rely on dedicated chemical pumps, pressure regulation systems, multiple flow sensors, electronic controls, and complex plumbing networks to monitor and control application rates.

These systems work well in large-scale agricultural environments, but they are often too complex, too expensive, and too difficult to integrate into the lawn care, landscape, and pest control markets.

From the beginning, DirectDraw™ pursued a different goal.

The objective was not to build a more complicated injection system. The objective was to build a simpler one. The KISS principle—Keep It Simple—was a core design philosophy from day one.

Instead of using chemical pumps and pressurized product tanks, DirectDraw™ utilizes the well-established Venturi effect to draw product directly from its container into the spray stream. The Venturi principle has been used throughout industry for decades and provides a reliable method of chemical induction without pumps, motors, or moving parts.

The challenge was never drawing the chemical.

The challenge was measuring it.

For decades, operators have been able to measure water flow with reasonable accuracy. Measuring the actual chemical being injected into the system, especially at the extremely low flow rates common in lawn care and pest control applications, proved far more difficult.

Many available flow measurement technologies were designed for laboratories, manufacturing facilities, or tightly controlled environments. When exposed to the realities of field use—including vibration, changing temperatures, varying viscosities, suspended particulates, and a wide range of product formulations—many technologies either lacked the required accuracy or failed to operate reliably.

For years, this limitation prevented the development of a practical direct-draw injection platform capable of accurately measuring actual chemical flow in real-world conditions.

That changed when new flow sensing technology became available.

Technology introduced in 2019 eventually provided the missing piece. After extensive evaluation and testing, it became possible to accurately monitor and verify chemical flow rates across a broad range of liquid products commonly used in lawn care, turf management, and pest control applications.

That breakthrough made DirectDraw™ possible.

The result is a system that combines the simplicity and reliability of Venturi-based chemical induction with real-time measurement of the chemical itself.

Why It Matters

Traditional systems typically measure water and estimate chemical.

DirectDraw™ measures the chemical itself.

Instead of relying solely on tank concentrations, dilution ratios, and assumptions, operators can directly observe the amount of product being injected into the spray stream in real time.

This provides:

- Real-time chemical flow verification

- Repeatable calibration

- Reduced guesswork

- Improved application accuracy

- Better documentation

- Reduced chemical waste

- Increased operator confidence

What The Patent Protects

U.S. Patent No. 12,515,180 B2 protects the DirectDraw™ approach to combining simple Venturi-based chemical induction with precision measurement and verification of the injected chemical stream.

The innovation is not the Venturi itself.

The innovation is making direct chemical measurement practical in the field while maintaining the simplicity, reliability, and affordability required by lawn care and pest control professionals.

While others focused on increasingly complex systems that relied on pumps, pressure regulation, and extensive electronic controls, DirectDraw™ pursued a different path: simplify the injection process while improving visibility into what is actually being applied.

After decades of estimating what should be happening, DirectDraw™ allows operators to measure what is actually happening.

The Industry Has Been Calibrating the Same Way for Decades

For decades, applicators have calibrated water flow and then calculated chemical rates.

The process works, but it is time-consuming and relies on multiple assumptions being correct throughout the application.

A typical calibration starts by filling the spray system with water and determining how much water is applied over a known area. The operator measures output, calculates gallons per acre or gallons per 1,000 square feet, and then uses those numbers to determine how much chemical should be added to the spray tank.

Once the calculations are complete, chemicals are batch mixed into the tank. From that point forward, the operator assumes the correct amount of chemical is being applied based on the original calibration.

But real-world conditions change.

Ground speed varies. Pressure changes. Nozzles wear. Flow rates fluctuate. Tank volumes can be estimated incorrectly. Product mixing errors happen. If something changes during the application, the actual chemical rate being applied may differ from the intended target.

Verifying the true chemical application rate often requires collecting samples, measuring volumes, performing calculations, or recalibrating the sprayer.

The industry has accepted this process because there has never been a practical way to directly measure the chemical itself while spraying.

What Makes DirectDraw™ Different?

Traditional systems measure water and estimate chemical.

DirectDraw™ measures the chemical itself, and changes the process by directly measuring the chemical being injected into the spray stream in real time.

Instead of estimating chemical application rates based on water flow calculations and tank concentrations, operators can see the actual chemical flow rate as it happens.

Need to verify a rate? Read the display.

Need to make an adjustment? Turn the dial and immediately see the change.

Need to confirm calibration? The system provides direct measurement of the injected product rather than relying solely on calculations.

By measuring the chemical itself, DirectDraw™ reduces the guesswork associated with traditional batch mixing and calibration procedures while giving operators a new level of visibility into their application system.

After decades of calculating what should be happening, DirectDraw™ allows operators to see what is actually happening.

DirectDraw™ approaches calibration from a different direction.

The operator only needs to know two things:

How long it takes to treat a known area.

How much product should be applied to that area.

An applicator determines their spray setup treats 1,000 square feet in 22 seconds.

The product label calls for 0.75 fluid ounces per 1,000 square feet.

Rather than calculating tank concentrations and batch mixes, DirectDraw™ simply converts the required application rate into a chemical flow rate.

0.75 fluid ounces equals approximately 22.2 milliliters.

If 22.2 milliliters must be applied in 22 seconds, the required injection rate becomes:

22.2 mL ÷ 22 sec × 60 sec/min = 60.5 mL/min

The operator then adjusts DirectDraw™ until the display reads approximately 60.5 mL/min.

Calibration complete.

No tank concentration calculations.

No determining how much product to add to 50, 100, or 200 gallons of water.

No estimating whether the correct amount of chemical is actually being injected.

The operator is directly measuring the chemical entering the spray stream in real time.

Need to change products?

Simply determine the required amount per 1,000 square feet, convert it to a target flow rate, and adjust the system accordingly.

For the first time, calibration can be based on the actual chemical being applied rather than assumptions about what should be happening inside a spray tank.

DirectDraw™ turns calibration from a batch-mixing exercise into a direct measurement process.

Bypass Pump Integration

DirectDraw™ integrates seamlessly with bypass-pump spray systems while preserving the pump's normal operating characteristics. In a bypass configuration, the pressure-relief return line is rerouted from the carrier tank to a point upstream of the pump and downstream of the DirectDraw™ injection system. This allows the pump to continuously circulate carrier fluid through the pump, maintaining stable system pressure and flow.

Because the bypass return is located after the DirectDraw™ injection point, only fresh carrier fluid entering the closed-loop system receives chemical injection before reaching the discharge outlet. The core DirectDraw™ process remains unchanged, requiring only slightly longer prime and purge times compared to demand-pump systems.

Traditional bypass systems often rely on continuous circulation to agitate tank mixes and keep products suspended. Since DirectDraw™ eliminates batch mixing and injects products on demand, tank agitation is no longer required. Operators can shut the pump off whenever spraying is not actively taking place, reducing unnecessary wear, lowering power consumption, and helping maintain proper operating temperatures.

Future Expansion: Product Manifold System

DirectDraw™ is being designed with future expansion in mind. A planned product manifold system will allow multiple products to remain connected, calibrated, and ready for use at all times.

With a simple flip of a selector valve, operators will be able to switch between products without changing settings or recalibrating the system. Simply purge the line, verify flow, and begin spraying. This approach can significantly reduce downtime between applications while maintaining the precision and flexibility that DirectDraw™ is designed to deliver.

Connect. Select. Purge. Spray.

Protected By U.S. Patent No. 12,515,180 B2

Direct Chemical Measurement Meets Simple Injection

Chemical injection is not a new concept.

For years, agricultural application equipment has used sophisticated direct-injection systems that meter concentrated products into a spray stream. Many of these systems rely on dedicated chemical pumps, pressure regulation systems, multiple flow sensors, electronic controls, and complex plumbing networks to monitor and control application rates.

These systems work well in large-scale agricultural environments, but they are often too complex, too expensive, and too difficult to integrate into the lawn care, landscape, and pest control markets.

From the beginning, DirectDraw™ pursued a different goal.

The objective was not to build a more complicated injection system. The objective was to build a simpler one. The KISS principle—Keep It Simple—was a core design philosophy from day one.

Instead of using chemical pumps and pressurized product tanks, DirectDraw™ utilizes the well-established Venturi effect to draw product directly from its container into the spray stream. The Venturi principle has been used throughout industry for decades and provides a reliable method of chemical induction without pumps, motors, or moving parts.

The challenge was never drawing the chemical.

The challenge was measuring it.

For decades, operators have been able to measure water flow with reasonable accuracy. Measuring the actual chemical being injected into the system, especially at the extremely low flow rates common in lawn care and pest control applications, proved far more difficult.

Many available flow measurement technologies were designed for laboratories, manufacturing facilities, or tightly controlled environments. When exposed to the realities of field use—including vibration, changing temperatures, varying viscosities, suspended particulates, and a wide range of product formulations—many technologies either lacked the required accuracy or failed to operate reliably.

For years, this limitation prevented the development of a practical direct-draw injection platform capable of accurately measuring actual chemical flow in real-world conditions.

That changed when new flow sensing technology became available.

Technology introduced in 2019 eventually provided the missing piece. After extensive evaluation and testing, it became possible to accurately monitor and verify chemical flow rates across a broad range of liquid products commonly used in lawn care, turf management, and pest control applications.

That breakthrough made DirectDraw™ possible.

The result is a system that combines the simplicity and reliability of Venturi-based chemical induction with real-time measurement of the chemical itself.

Traditional systems typically measure water and estimate chemical.

DirectDraw™ measures the chemical itself.

Instead of relying solely on tank concentrations, dilution ratios, and assumptions, operators can directly observe the amount of product being injected into the spray stream in real time.

Real-time chemical flow verification

Repeatable calibration

Reduced guesswork

Improved application accuracy

Better documentation

Reduced chemical waste

Increased operator confidence

What The Patent Protects

U.S. Patent No. 12,515,180 B2 protects the DirectDraw™ approach to combining simple Venturi-based chemical induction with precision measurement and verification of the injected chemical stream.

The innovation is not the Venturi itself.

The innovation is making direct chemical measurement practical in the field while maintaining the simplicity, reliability, and affordability required by lawn care and pest control professionals.

While others focused on increasingly complex systems that relied on pumps, pressure regulation, and extensive electronic controls, DirectDraw™ pursued a different path: simplify the injection process while improving visibility into what is actually being applied.

After decades of estimating what should be happening, DirectDraw™ allows operators to measure what is actually happening.

Traditional Systems

Measure water → Calculate dilution → Estimate chemical application

Measure the chemical itself → Verify application in real time

That difference is the foundation for improved calibration, reduced waste, better documentation, greater accountability, and measurable ROI.

DIRECTDRAW™ COMPLETE ROI ANALYSIS

How DirectDraw™ Can Pay For Itself In A Single Season

DirectDraw™ was developed to eliminate many of the inefficiencies that have existed in spray operations for decades. Traditional batch-mixing systems require operators to measure chemicals, mix tanks, maintain agitation, estimate application rates, transport large volumes of premixed solution, and repeatedly return to the shop for refills. Each of these activities consumes time, introduces error, increases operating costs, and reduces the amount of productive work completed during the day.

DirectDraw™ changes the workflow by measuring and injecting concentrate directly into the spray stream while providing real-time monitoring of actual chemical flow. The result is a system that can improve chemical accuracy, reduce labor, increase production capacity, lower operating costs, improve recordkeeping, and reduce environmental risk.

projects.ai_description_en:
The DirectDraw™ Precision Injection System is a breakthrough real-time chemical measurement and delivery technology for professional lawn and landscape operators. Instead of the traditional process of pre-mixing chemicals in tanks—which involves measuring, mixing, calibrating, cleaning enormous equipment, and dealing with product waste—DirectDraw™ allows operators to draw only what they need, directly from the source, when they need it. The system directly measures chemical flow into the spray stream in real time, giving operators precise visibility and control over application rates without relying on dilution ratios or assumptions.

At the heart of DirectDraw™ is patented microflow measurement technology (U.S. Patent No. 12,515,180 B2) that accurately monitors and verifies chemical injection across virtually all liquid products, regardless of viscosity, formulation, or suspended particulate content. The system features integrated bypass pump technology and a live monitoring/calibration sensor, enabling operators to make immediate adjustments and confirm application rates with confidence—eliminating calibration uncertainty entirely. An additional Product Manifold System is also in the pipeline for future expansion, allowing even greater flexibility in multi-product operations.

Why DirectDraw™ matters is simple: it transforms the economics of spray contracting. By eliminating batch mixing, operators reclaim significant production time currently lost to tank draining, rinsing, measuring, recalibrating, and rebatching chemicals. The shift translates directly into more billable hours on route, less idle time at the shop, and the ability to add capacity without adding headcount. With the Founders Edition limited to just 40 systems at $3,199 (estimated delivery: October 2026), DirectDraw™ offers early supporters a first production batch allocation and Founders Edition recognition as the system moves from completed prototyping into full manufacturing, with production scale tied directly to campaign success.

Conclusion: the DirectDraw™ Precision Injection System is not a concept—it is a fully engineered, prototyped, and validated platform ready to replace decades-old batch mixing methods with precision injection. By directly measuring chemical flow in real time, eliminating waste, and freeing operators from the time sink of equipment cleaning and recalibration, DirectDraw™ promises to fundamentally increase profitable production time for lawn and landscape professionals. The campaign exists to fund the initial manufacturing run, scale production, and place these systems into operator hands sooner.

## Story

As Parents and  Electronics Design Team with over 10 years of experience, we know the daily struggle: chaotic mornings, screen-fueled bedtime battles, and the toll it takes on kids' sleep, eyesight, and routines. Traditional alarms are harsh; screens are addictive. So we asked: what if we could create more than just an alarm clock?

The answer is PRUNUS — a purpose-built Pomodoro timer and daily routine tool designed exclusively for children. After months of research into kids' learning focus and sleep habits, we independently developed the hardware, timing logic, and kid-friendly operating system. It helps children build healthy time management habits: focused study with the Pomodoro technique, regular rest reminders, and consistent sleep schedules — all through a gentle bedside companion that tells stories, answers questions, and plays music, helping kids naturally let go of screen dependence.

#### ✅ Core Functions (Main Features)

1. Custom Pomodoro Timer: Multiple preset time modes for kids’ study, reading and break. We designed all timing modes based on child psychology.

2. Sleep Schedule Management: Built-in countdown mode helps children develop regular bedtime habits.

3. Simple & Safe Hardware Design: Ergonomic shape and easy-to-use buttons, fully designed and tested by our team for young children.

✅ Auxiliary Voice Features

This device is equipped with a basic voice module powered by AI technology. This is only a secondary supporting function, not the core of the product.

projects.ai_description_en:
**PRUNUS T05 – Smart Pomodoro Clock for Kids**

PRUNUS T05 is a smart Pomodoro timer and sleep-routine manager designed exclusively for children. Created by parents and an electronics design team with over 10 years of experience, it tackles the everyday struggles of chaotic mornings, screen-fueled bedtime battles, and the strain that takes on kids’ focus, eyesight, and daily routines. Instead of harsh traditional alarms and addictive screens, PRUNUS offers a gentle bedside companion that helps children develop healthy time-management habits. It combines custom Pomodoro timers, built-in bedtime countdowns, and a cute retro design into one kid-friendly device—free from full-screen distractions.

At its core, PRUNUS offers **custom Pomodoro study timers** with multiple preset modes for focused work, reading, and rest, all based on child psychology. Its **sleep schedule management** uses a countdown mode to ease children into consistent bedtimes, while a compact, rounded design with ergonomic buttons makes it safe and easy for small hands to operate independently. The vivid gradient LED display shows real-time clock and timing info, and a rotating top control knob adds a tactile, playful interaction. Available in two retro-chic colorways (classic red and soft blue) with rounded edges and a cute tripod foot stand, PRUNUS fits naturally into a child’s bedside environment.

What sets PRUNUS apart is its exclusive focus on a screen-free healthy lifestyle for kids, without radical reinvention. It is built from durable, food-grade ABS material, has passed rigorous safety tests (power, heat resistance, drop, and battery), and emphasizes recyclable and biodegradable materials where possible. By weaving together simple interaction, comforting bedtime routines, and gentle distraction-free guidance, PRUNUS helps reduce screen dependence and fosters independence in learning and sleeping habits. Paired with a thoughtful design that prioritizes safety and ease of use over complexity, PRUNUS aims to be a long-lasting sleep and focus companion for children who need more calm, less stimulation, and a better rhythm to their daily life.

**#ScreenFreeGrowth – the ultimate gentle Pomodoro alarm clock that nurtures focus, calm, and independent routines.**

The project is not a finished consumer product; features are experimental and redesigns are expected. The creator commits to transparent communication and incremental testing.

Campaign Rewards FAQ 9 Updates 0 Comments 0 Community Campaign Rewards Creator FAQ 9 Updates 0 Comments 0 Community Back this project Remind me Story THE LIGHT TELLS YOU SOMETHING IS WRONG. DRIVEPULSE TELLS YOU WHAT. A check-engine lamp is one bit of information. On or off. Something, somewhere, is wrong — go pay someone to find out what. DrivePulse watches the ECU continuously. The instant a fault is flagged, it pulls the code and prints it in words. On your dash. Before your phone has even unlocked. P0301 becomes Cylinder 1 Misfire. No app. No account. No cloud. No subscription. Nothing that can be switched off on you. It is called HAX DrivePulse . HAX is the name I build under, and it is stamped into every unit and drawn on every screen. IT NAMES THE FAULT 355 trouble codes are described on the device itself. No internet, no lookup, no phone. And when a code is not in the table, it still decodes to the right area of the car — P1E22 comes back as Powertrain, manufacturer-specific rather than leaving you with a five-character riddle. Current, pending and permanent codes. The freeze-frame snapshot of exactly what the engine was doing the moment the fault hit — RPM, speed, coolant, load. And a deliberate two-step erase that warns you it also resets your smog monitors, because that is the mistake everyone makes once. EVERY VALUE, THREE WAYS Any value can be a big number, a gauge, or a scrolling graph. Hold NEXT to switch. Your coolant temperature as a number while you watch it climb, as a graph when you want to know whether it is still climbing. EIGHTEEN LIVE SENSORS RPM, speed, coolant, load, short and long fuel trims, intake pressure and temperature, airflow, throttle, battery voltage, fuel level, fuel rate and more — whatever your vehicle exposes. Plus a trip computer, instant and average economy, range, peak records, a 0-60 timer, and configurable overheat, low-voltage and shift alerts. If your car does not provide a value, DrivePulse says so instead of inventing one. TWO BUTTONS DRIVE ALL OF IT Two physical buttons. No touchscreen to hunt through at 70 mph, no menu that needs you to look away for four seconds. NEXT moves, SELECT picks, holding either one does the bigger thing. Metric or imperial. Set it once.  ONE SCREEN, OR FOUR HAX DrivePulse SOLO — one configurable OLED. The whole instrument in something the size of a matchbox. HAX DrivePulse QUAD — four OLEDs. One interactive screen, three assignable live-data screens. RPM, coolant, battery and speed all readable in a single glance, without pressing anything. WHY NOT JUST USE YOUR PHONE Phone apps read OBD-II fine. But a phone is not a dashboard instrument. It has to be mounted, unlocked, connected and charged. It rings. It overheats in summer sun. It is the thing you are supposed to not be looking at. DrivePulse does one job. It stays in the car, reconnects to its saved adapter, and is ready when the engine turns over. SMOG-CHECK READY See whether your emissions monitors are complete before you drive to the inspection — not after you have paid for a failed one. And get warned that erasing codes resets them.  SAFE BY DESIGN Standard OBD-II reads, plus the same clear command every scan tool uses. It cannot flash, tune, or write to your ECU. It reads. That is the whole surface area. COMPATIBILITY DrivePulse is for OBD-II vehicles, including US-market cars from model year 1996 onward. It needs a Bluetooth Low Energy ELM327 adapter — classic Bluetooth-only and WiFi-only adapters are not supported by the current firmware. Vehicle support varies. Not every car exposes every PID, and inexpensive ELM327 clones vary in quality. A tested-adapter list goes up before fulfillment. ZERO SCREWS. EVERYTHING SNAPS. I grew up in a working-class Mexican family in Oak Cliff, Dallas, where fixing something was usually more realistic than replacing it. My dad was an electrician. Tools, wiring and troubleshooting were normal household objects. So DrivePulse opens with a fingernail. Two printed parts, snap-fit, no glue and no pile of screws. Boards clip into printed trays. The caps push on last. I plan to sell every spare part — caps, panels, boards — close to cost. A cracked cap should be a cheap problem, not a dead device. And because there is no server behind it, nothing I do or ever stop doing can switch your DrivePulse off. WHAT WORKS TODAY, AND WHAT DOES NOT YET I would rather you back this knowing exactly where it stands. Working right now, in the video and photos on this page: ESP32-C3 firmware, BLE adapter discovery and automatic reconnect Live OBD-II data across all 18 sensors The full code reader, with 355 plain-language descriptions Freeze frame, smog readiness, trip computer, alerts One to four physical screens Both Solo and Quad built and running in two different vehicles Not done yet: Final enclosure and vehicle-fit testing Locking the bill of materials and backup suppliers Assembly fixtures and a repeatable build checklist Batch programming, burn-in and vehicle-simulator testing Packaging, documentation and replacement-part stock That is what the $9,500 is for. It is a small goal because it is an honest one — components, printing, packaging, test gear, fees, and a reserve for the parts that arrive broken. Firmware updates are free for the life of the product , over USB-C. If a bug turns up after shipping, I fix it and you flash it. On the roadmap, not in this campaign: the ESP32-C3 has WiFi on board, so wireless updating is something I want to build. It is not written yet, it is not what your pledge is funding, and I am not putting a date on it. USB-C updates are what ships. FIRMWARE AND OPEN SOURCE The firmware is proprietary at launch. I am not offering the source code as part of this campaign. I would like to open parts of the project in future, but I cannot responsibly promise when while I am still building the first business around it. Back this for the product described here, not for a future open-source release. WHO IS BUILDING THIS My name is Valdemar Gonzalez. I am 23, an electrical engineering student at UT Arlington, raised in Oak Cliff. I have built with ESP32s, CAN bus, GPS, environmental sensors, OLEDs and printed enclosures for years — an intelligent air-conditioner controller, an OBD-II fault monitor, a hiking GPS companion, automotive gauges, large interactive displays. Most of them started the same way: I wanted something that did not exist, cost too much, or was needlessly hard to use. DrivePulse is the first one I am seriously preparing to manufacture, and the first to carry the HAX mark. It also became important to me during a hard stretch of my life. Engineering gave me somewhere to put the energy: solve one problem, repair one circuit, rewrite one function, redesign one enclosure feature, and make something work that had not worked the day before. Every prototype on this page is late nights, wrong components, and code that got thrown away and written again. I am not a company with a factory. I am one person with working hardware, a finished design, and a realistic first production run. Something built at a desk in Oak Cliff can end up on dashboards everywhere. Sometimes the hardest season of your life is where you start building the next one. SEE EVERYTHING Full screen gallery, the manual and build details: https://drivepulse-by-hax.pages.dev/

projects.name: ARANYA: Building Our First Functional Prototype
projects.blurb: Help us turn a sensory refuge concept into a physical, testable prototype integrating structure, light, sound, and control.
projects.ai_intro_en: ARANYA is a modular sensory refuge designed for small spaces, integrating a corner structure, seat, ambient light, sound, and physical control to create a personal retreat for pause, meditation, or focus. This campaign funds the development of the first functional prototype to test and validate the concept, not a finished product.
ai_highlights_en: Modular corner refuge combining seat, light, sound, and control for small homes.
Prototype campaign: backers support the development journey, not a preorder.
Transparent process with digital rewards, journals, and prototype demo invites.
ai_specs_en: Full-size corner structure and seat; dimensions and materials TBD
Experimental LED system with warm/cool tones and basic modes
Speaker system with ambient sound library; placement and clarity testing
Physical controller prototype with buttons and simple display
Early experiments with shelves, pockets, attachment points
Power distribution and wiring in development
To be validated through physical testing
Subject to testing and safety evaluation
projects.ai_risks_en: Technical integration of structure, lighting, sound, and control may require multiple iterations. Dimensions, stability, comfort, and electronics are unvalidated and may change substantially. Schedule delays possible due to material availability and specialist timelines. Completing the prototype does not guarantee commercial production. Functions may be modified or removed for safety or budget reasons.
projects.ai_creator_bio_en: ARANYA is being developed in Mérida, Mexico, led by Tomas Navarrete, with specialized support in industrial design, carpentry, electronics, and software.

projects.name: LabStocker - Real-time lab inventory device & software
projects.blurb: Fundraising to complete working prototype of user-input consumption and re-stocking lab inventory system.
projects.hw_reason: Lab inventory device with electronic components
projects.ai_intro_en: LabStocker is a real-time lab inventory device and software system that captures user input to update stock levels instantly, eliminating the need for manual spreadsheets or printed labels. It provides location tagging, alerts for low/high stock, perishable dates, and exportable data for purchase orders, helping labs reduce waste, over/under-stocking, and downtime.
ai_highlights_en: Real-time stock updates via device and software, eliminating manual tracking.
Self-installable with adhesive backing; no extra equipment required.
Reduces waste and downtime with alerts, exportable data, and location tagging.
ai_specs_en: Clear LCD display with custom text locations
Bluetooth or WiFi signal to main receiver
Self-adhesive backing and adjustable clamp for edge of shelves
Exportable data easily translatable to purchase orders
projects.ai_risks_en: The primary risk is potential cost overruns for device and software development, though the creator has obtained multiple quotes to minimize this. The project is being developed full-time, and market research indicates demand across various facilities with on-site inventory.
projects.ai_creator_bio_en: Kirk has over 10 years of laboratory management experience, focusing on solutions to make lab management easier and more automated.
